proofs.proof_tex:
Consider first an arbitrary instance in the class of the first sentence. Because \(\mathcal C(G,s)\neq\varnothing\), fix \(R_0\in\mathcal C(G,s)\). The residual \(R_0\) is nonempty by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}singleton\mbox{-}hedges}\), because its originating hedge strictly contains \(\{s\}\). Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\mbox{-}rational\mbox{-}cost}\) and finiteness give
\[
 c_{\min}:=\min_{v\in R_0}c(v)>0.
\]
For every vector \(y\) feasible for Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}covering\mbox{-}lp}\), nonnegativity of its coordinates and the constraint for \(R_0\) imply
\[
 \sum_{v\in V^{-}}c(v)y_v
 \geq \sum_{v\in R_0}c(v)y_v
 \geq c_{\min}\sum_{v\in R_0}y_v
 \geq c_{\min}>0.
\]
The all-ones vector is feasible, so the LP feasible set is nonempty; it is a closed subset of the compact cube \([0,1]^{V^{-}}\), and the objective is continuous. Thus its minimum exists and
\[
 \operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\geq c_{\min}>0.
\]
Moreover, if \(A\) is feasible for Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}mcid\mbox{-}objective}\), its incidence vector is LP-feasible and has objective \(\sum_{v\in A}c(v)\). Taking minima gives
\[
 \operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq \operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c).
\]

The hypotheses just imposed are precisely within the weighted promised-rank scope of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}rounding}\). That theorem constructs a feasible intervention \(A_t\) satisfying
\[
 \sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)\leq 2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c).
\]
By the minimizing definition of \(\operatorname{OPT}\),
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)
 \leq \sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)
 \leq 2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c).
\]
Division by the strictly positive LP value therefore yields
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)}{\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)}\leq 2
\]
for every positive-rational-cost instance in the asserted class. This establishes the universal upper bound without a unit-cost or bidirected-radius restriction.

For the matching lower bound, fix \(n\geq2\), take \(H=K_n\) with any total order on its vertices, form its private-guard expansion \(G_{K_n}\), and put unit cost on every vertex in \(V^{-}\). Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\) shows that this is a finite simple bow-free acyclic singleton-target instance, that its bidirected subgraph is a tree of radius at most two, and that
\[
 \mathcal C(G_{K_n},s)
 =\bigl\{\{x_u,x_v,z_{\{u,v\}}\}:\{u,v\}\in E(K_n)\bigr\}.
\]
In particular the clutter is nonempty and its residual rank is three. Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}objective\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}hardness}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G_{K_n},s,c)=\tau(K_n)=n-1,
\]
where the last equality holds because omitting two vertices of \(K_n\) leaves their joining edge uncovered, while all but one vertex form a cover.

Set \(y_{x_u}=1/2\) for every \(u\in U\) and \(y_{z_e}=0\) for every \(e\in E(K_n)\). Each residual constraint has left side \(1/2+1/2+0=1\), so this vector is feasible and
\[
 \operatorname{LP}(G_{K_n},s,c)\leq \frac n2.
\]
Conversely, let \(y\) be any feasible fractional vector. Summing the constraint
\[
 y_{x_u}+y_{x_v}+y_{z_e}\geq1
\]
over all \(e=\{u,v\}\in E(K_n)\), and using that every vertex of \(K_n\) has degree \(n-1\), gives
\[
 (n-1)\sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}+\sum_{e\in E(K_n)}y_{z_e}
 \geq \binom n2.
\]
After division by \(n-1>0\),
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}
 +\frac1{n-1}\sum_{e\in E(K_n)}y_{z_e}
 \geq \frac n2.
\]
Since \(n\geq2\), nonnegativity of \(y\) implies
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}+\sum_{e\in E(K_n)}y_{z_e}
 \geq
 \sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}
 +\frac1{n-1}\sum_{e\in E(K_n)}y_{z_e}
 \geq\frac n2.
\]
This is the unit-cost LP objective, so the upper and lower bounds coincide:
\[
 \operatorname{LP}(G_{K_n},s,c)=\frac n2,
 \qquad
 \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G_{K_n},s,c)}{\operatorname{LP}(G_{K_n},s,c)}
 =\frac{n-1}{n/2}=2-\frac2n.
\]
Every member of this sequence belongs to the broader weighted class, and \(2-2/n\to2\). Combined with the universal upper bound, this proves that the weighted integrality-gap supremum is exactly two.

Finally assume \(\mathsf{UGC}\) as in Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}unique\mbox{-}games}\), and fix \(\epsilon>0\). Suppose, toward a contradiction, that a polynomial-time \((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation exists for the narrower subclass in the final sentence. Given a finite simple source graph \(H=(U,E)\) with \(E\neq\varnothing\), form the unit-cost private-guard expansion \(G_H\). Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\) puts \(G_H\) in that subclass. If the alleged algorithm returns a feasible intervention \(A\), Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}objective\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}hardness}\) replaces every selected guard by an endpoint of its source edge and produces, in polynomial time, a vertex cover \(C_A\) satisfying
\[
 |C_A|\leq |A|
 \leq (2-\epsilon)\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)
 =(2-\epsilon)\tau(H).
\]
If \(E=\varnothing\), the empty set is an optimal vertex cover, so this exceptional case is also handled in polynomial time. We would therefore obtain a polynomial-time \((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation for Minimum Vertex Cover on arbitrary finite simple graphs, contradicting Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}ugc\mbox{-}vertex\mbox{-}cover\mbox{-}hardness}\). Hence the claimed approximation does not exist under \(\mathsf{UGC}\).

proposed.statement: The supremum of \(\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)/\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\), taken over all positive-rational-cost finite simple bow-free singleton-target ADMG instances satisfying \(r(G,s)\leq 3\) and \(\mathcal C(G,s)\neq\varnothing\), is exactly two. For the unit-cost private-guard expansion \(G_{K_n}\), where \(n\geq 2\), the ratio is \(2-2/n\). Under \(\mathsf{UGC}\), for every fixed \(\epsilon>0\), there is no polynomial-time \((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation for \(\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\) even on the narrower subclass of unit-cost rank-three instances whose bidirected subgraph is a tree of radius at most two.
proposed.justification: The weighted rank-three upper bound and a matching unit-cost sequence certify that two is the exact natural-LP integrality-gap supremum on the full positive-rational-cost promised class; the conditional algorithmic lower bound already holds on a substantially narrower subclass.
proposed.gap: Khot and Regev establish the approximation threshold for Vertex Cover, and Singh characterizes the source LP gap; no published result transfers the exact weighted gap or the conditional threshold to a bounded-rank causal-effect-identification design class.
proposed.consumer: Algorithm designers may use the weighted factor-two guarantee for every positive-rational-cost instance supplied with the rank-three promise, while treating it as worst-case optimal under \(\mathsf{UGC}\) even on unit-cost radius-two bidirected-tree instances.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The active orchestrator directive requires the integrality-gap equality to range over the full positive-rational-cost rank-three class, while retaining the UGC lower bound on the narrower unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass. The replacement also declares the primitive graph and cost assumptions used directly by the strengthened proof.

prose_updates.tldr: Rank three is the first nonzero minimal residual-hedge rank for bow-free singleton-target ADMGs. Four-vertex hedges are exactly complementary directed and bidirected spanning paths. A one-private-guard expansion realizes the edge clutter of every ordered simple graph exactly, yielding unit-cost NP and APX hardness on radius-two bidirected trees. Under the promise \(r(G,s)\leq 3\), the path classification partitions every minimal residual across target parents and spouses; after polynomial enumeration under that promise, this yields a deterministic weighted factor-two LP rounding algorithm. The weighted natural-covering-LP integrality-gap supremum is exactly two over all positive-rational-cost finite simple bow-free singleton-target instances with nonempty residual clutter and rank at most three; unit-cost complete-graph expansions on radius-two bidirected trees attain \(2-2/n\), and the Khot--Regev \((2-\epsilon)\) threshold transfers under \(\mathsf{UGC}\) already on that narrower subclass. Promised enumeration and an optimizer-or-rank-violation interface connect the theorem to existing exact solvers, while unrestricted rank-three recognition remains an explicit open question.

project_justification.gap: The published MCID frontier jumps from polynomial solvability at residual size two to unrestricted logarithmic hardness. It does not identify the first nonempty bow-free singleton rank, give a weighted constant-factor algorithm there, or determine the natural covering relaxation's exact integrality-gap supremum on the full positive-rational-cost rank-three class.
project_justification.niche: Rank-three hedge clutters are not arbitrary three-uniform clutters: every residual crosses the target-parent and target-spouse partition. That structure yields weighted factor-two rounding for every positive-rational-cost promised instance, while private guards make even the unit-cost radius-two-bidirected-tree subclass expressive enough to transfer graph vertex-cover lower bounds.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the exact four-vertex obstruction classification and private-guard representation theorem, transfers objective-preserving hardness, establishes that the weighted natural-covering-LP integrality-gap supremum is exactly two on all positive-rational-cost nonempty rank-three instances, and proves the matching \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional approximation barrier on a narrower unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass. It also gives a certifying interface useful without asserting an unrestricted rank recognizer.

prose_updates.related_work: Shpitser and Pearl supply the complete hedge obstruction used to interpret residual hitting as causal identification. Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash formulate MCID as minimum-weight hedge hitting, prove unrestricted hardness, and settle bounded residual size through two; their Appendix D.2 is the direct boundary this paper continues. Elahi and coauthors replace explicit hedge enumeration by WPMAX-SAT and ILP and leave approximation algorithms open, making their RC2 and Gurobi workflow the immediate computational consumer. Nemhauser and Trotter provide the classical half-integral vertex-cover geometry that informs the rounding argument, although the parent-spouse threshold proof is stated directly on causal residuals and applies to arbitrary positive rational weights under the rank-three promise. Alimonti and Kann provide cubic vertex-cover APX hardness, and Khot and Regev provide the conditional factor-two lower bound transferred by the exact private-guard realization to the unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass. Singh's source-LP gap formula motivates the complete-graph lower-bound sequence; the present result combines that sequence with weighted causal rounding to determine the supremum over the larger positive-rational-cost rank-three class. Fernau's explicit-hypergraph branching informs only the scoped bounded-cardinality routine.
